author: Ralph Macchio’s Sandwich
title: Fun and Engaging!
content: This is the most complex, satisfying and engaging game I’ve come across in nearly two full decades of mobile gaming.  The gameplay mechanics are vast and varied, the rewards are satisfying, and the strategy is stimulating.  Aside from personal and individual quests and rewards, of which there are so many, you also get another level of engagement by playing as part of an Alliance.  Through the alliance you can access additional accomplishments, achievements, and rewards that are not possible for a solo player.  Additionally, I have found the online community and my alliance to be friendly, helpful, and fun.    While there seem to be many generally accepted best practices for progression established in the online community, you are still free to “go rogue” and make personal progression decisions based on your own preferences and goals.  This allows for a wide variety of player types and widens the variety of encounters you can run across in battle.    Overall I can see this game being a mainstay in my mobile gaming for a long time to come.  Very satisfied with everything so far and a glad that I got an ad for this game in some other, less amazing game!

What I Love About It:
 Rewarding Progression: Hitting level 22 takes genuine time and planning, but seeing your squad power and hero lineup scale up makes every upgrade feel earned.
 Hero & Squad Synergy: Powering up heroes and pairing them with strong troop tiers gives you a real competitive edge in battles.
 Alliance Play: Having a solid military build makes you an asset in alliance events and territory control.
My Advice for New Players:
Don't just rush your HQ—put in the work on your base research, keep your heroes upgraded, and train your troops constantly. Build that strong foundation early, and you'll be a force to be reckoned with!

author: Instman
title: Money grab
content:
Do not waste your time or money on this game until the developers start listening! 

Z Route: Redemption has become one of the most frustrating and unfair mobile games I have ever played. 

Players who spend hundreds or even tens of thousands of dollars Building heroes, upgrading gear, Increasing skills, And raising overall strength only to watch accounts 2 million power plus under them beat them in 1V1 battles. 

What exactly are we paying for?

Multiple players have documented these ridiculous matchups with screenshots, stats, gear comparisons, and even video recordings. Instead of seriously addressing the imbalance, the developers give generic responses that essentially boiled down to keep upgrading, keep spending, and keep trying.

That is unacceptable.

The problem is even worse when newer servers get matched with older servers that have had access to Features, upgrades, bonuses, and progression systems that the newer servers haven’t even had the opportunity to obtain yet! How is that even remotely balanced competition?

Players are not asking to automatically win because we spent money. We are asking for the upgrades, power rankings, stats, gear, and progression systems advertised by the game to actually matter.

If a player has invested thousands of dollars and built a team that is millions of power stronger, there should be a clear, understandable gameplay reason when a dramatically weaker opponent destroys that team. if the displayed numbers do not accurately represent combat effective, then explain what does.

Now players, and even an entire servers, are starting to boycott ALL spending because complaints are going nowhere.

No packs. No upgrades. No $5 purchases. NOTHING! 

When you’re paying customers are organizing spending boycotts just to get the developers to acknowledge serious balancing concerns, something has gone terribly wrong.

author: Ashley Loveland
title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ The Best Game I’ve Ever Played — ZRoute: Redemption
content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ The Best Game I’ve Ever Played — ZRoute: Redemption

ZRoute: Redemption is hands down one of the best games I have ever played! From the amazing graphics and immersive world to the intriguing storyline, challenging missions, and endless things to do, this game truly keeps you coming back for more. There is always something happening, and it never gets boring!

One of my favorite parts is the alliance system. It’s so much more than simply joining a group of players. You actually build relationships, communicate through chat, help one another, contribute to alliance goals, and work together to accomplish missions. My alliance honestly feels more like a family than a group of strangers. Players genuinely look out for each other, and the teamwork makes the game so much more enjoyable.

The variety of events is another huge plus. There are always new challenges and activities that keep things exciting and give you something to work toward. With so many different options available, you can play in different ways and never feel like you’re doing the exact same thing over and over.

I also love the social aspect. Being able to chat and interact with players from all over the world has allowed me to make friendships I probably never would have made otherwise. It’s incredible how a game can bring people from completely different places together and create such a strong sense of community.

The customer service is excellent, too. Even more impressive is that the creators actually seem to listen to their players. They are open to ideas and suggestions and willing to consider ways to incorporate player feedback into the game. That makes you feel like your voice matters and that the people behind ZRoute: Redemption genuinely care about making the game better.

The graphics, storyline, missions, events, alliances, friendships, teamwork, and incredible amount of content all come together to create an experience that is truly special. There are so many options and so much to explore, and the game constantly gives you reasons to keep playing.

If you’re looking for a game that offers action, strategy, teamwork, competition, community, and friendships, I absolutely recommend giving ZRoute: Redemption a try.

5 stars without hesitation! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

ZRoute: Redemption isn’t just a game to me anymore—it’s a community, an adventure, and a family. 🧟‍♀️🍻🔥

title: Отличная игра!
content:
Очень достойная игра, которая реально затягивает. Сначала скачал просто попробовать, а в итоге незаметно для себя начал заходить каждый день.
Понравилось, что здесь есть не только развитие базы, но и много других механик: герои, отряды, исследования, события, альянсы и взаимодействие с другими игроками. Постоянно есть чем заняться, поэтому игра не превращается в однообразное «зашёл — собрал ресурсы — вышел».
Отдельно хочется отметить атмосферу. Тематика зомби-апокалипсиса отлично сочетается со стратегическим геймплеем, а развитие своей базы и команды действительно создаёт ощущение, что ты постепенно строишь собственное выжившее поселение.

В целом Z Route: Redemption приятно удивила. Если нравятся стратегии, развитие базы и зомби-тематика — однозначно стоит попробовать. Лично для меня одна из тех игр, которые устанавливаешь «на пару минут», а потом обнаруживаешь, что уже прошёл час.

Разработчикам респект, буду продолжать играть! 🔥

author: Blreed44
title: Just one last mission…famous last words
content:
Z Route: Redemption is one of those games that’s easy to pick up and surprisingly hard to put down. The zombie setting pulls you in, but it’s the progression, strategy, and constant “just one more run” feeling that keeps you playing.
I really like that the game doesn’t feel completely mindless—you actually have to think about your upgrades, weapons, and how you approach each situation. There’s a satisfying sense of getting stronger and better as you play, and when a run finally comes together, it feels earned.
The biggest compliment I can give Z Route: Redemption is that I’ve caught myself opening it to play for a few minutes and realizing WAY more time has passed than I intended. 😂
Fun, addictive, challenging without being frustrating, and definitely worth giving a shot. I’m looking forward to seeing what gets added next! Find me: Reeder

author: Smh23421
title: More Than Just a Strategy Game
content:
Z Route Redemption has a good mix of strategy, competition, and teamwork that keeps the game interesting. There’s always something going on, from the different weekly events and VS competitions to Glory Trials, Arena, and the extended Zombie Exploration. The events give you different ways to play, earn extra rewards, and keep progressing without everything feeling the same every week.

Getting into the right alliance is also a huge part of the experience. Other players can teach you things, help you grow, and make the game a lot more enjoyable. The conversations and friendships that come from being in an active alliance can turn a mobile game into a little internet family of people you actually look forward to playing with.

There’s definitely a learning curve, especially when you’re starting out, but there’s always something new to learn and work toward. It’s not perfect, but between the events, competition, strategy, and community, there are plenty of reasons to keep coming back. If you enjoy strategy games where the people you play with matter just as much as the game itself, Z Route Redemption is worth checking out

author: Just a dodo bird
title: Go broke (or stop playing)
content:
Z Route has better graphics and better gameplay than a lot of similar games—at least for the first 10 levels.

However the deeper you go, the less it will let you play without spending money—a lot of money.

At first, the game is pretty generous with rewards and resources. Certain conditions have to be met to keep actually playing. (It involves gathering the resources and building prerequisite buildings in order to level up.)

For the first 10 levels this goes pretty quickly, but by level 11, you either have to wait 5 or more hours to keep playing or pay fairly large fees that would probably run as much as USD 40-USD 60 to keep playing without major interruptions.

Now there are people who might argue that the interruptions are good. Keeping a player from becoming addicted, but it only does this for those willing to take the interruptions. For those who can’t, the cost could be exorbitant, even ruinous.

If you are the type of person who can take the interruptions then it’s a fun game. If you don’t have the patience for that best not to play or to play the first 10 levels then delete the game.
